title: Australian regulators raise compliance concerns over agent commission ban
summary_en: Australia’s higher education and vocational education regulators have issued a joint sector alert warning providers over practices that may undermine a ban on education agent commissions linked to onshore overseas student transfers.
author: Kim Martin
title_cn: Australian regulators raise compliance concerns over agent commission ban

title: Made Impact aims to “change the narrative” with UN summit
summary_en: The inaugural Made Impact Summit 2026 will take place at the United Nations in New York, it has been confirmed.
author: Nicholas Cuthbert
title_cn: Made Impact aims to “change the narrative” with UN summit

title: White House proposal to “dramatically weaken” US research, experts warn
summary_en: US higher education leaders are calling on Congress to reject a Trump administration proposal to hand political appointees control over federal grantmaking, potentially impacting $1.1 trillion in funding.
author: Polly Nash
title_cn: White House proposal to “dramatically weaken” US research, experts warn

title: UK unis must pivot towards partnerships as China market evolves
summary_en: UK universities must move beyond viewing China as a recruitment market and instead build deeper strategic partnerships if they are to remain competitive, delegates heard at the British Universities China Association's (BUCA) ninth annual conference.
author: Rongrong Walker
title_cn: UK unis must pivot towards partnerships as China market evolves

title: Every 10 international students generate £1m for UK economy
summary_en: International students represent a major economic benefit to the UK, generating billions during their time in the country, a new report has found.
author: Beth Kennedy
title_cn: Every 10 international students generate £1m for UK economy

title: Erasmus+ to replace Turing and Taith as sector calls for best of both
summary_en: As the UK winds down Turing and Taith in favour of a more generously funded Erasmus+, stakeholders say the transition must preserve the former schemes' successes.
author: Polly Nash
title_cn: Erasmus+ to replace Turing and Taith as sector calls for best of both
